title: Two Elections, Two Ballots: What Laredo Voters Need to Know Before Dec. 5 and Dec. 12
excerpt: Laredo voters are heading into an unusual December: two separate elections, on two separate ballots, in the space of one week. Early voting is already underway
content:
Laredo voters are heading into an unusual December: two separate elections, on two separate ballots, in the space of one week. Early voting is already underway for one of them, and confusion over the two races is the first thing election officials want voters to clear up.

Early voting began Monday, Nov. 23, in the special election for Laredo City Council District VIII. Election officials reported 257 ballots cast on the first day, including 185 in-person votes and 72 mail-in ballots. Voters can cast a ballot at any of four sites: the Webb County Elections Office at 720 Convent Ave., Lamar Bruni Vergara Inner City Park at 202 W. Plum St., Laredo Fire Department No. 1 at 1 Guadalupe St., and Gallagher Garden Apartments at 5118 Gallagher Ave.

The remaining early voting schedule for the District VIII race is Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Wednesday, Nov. 25, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.; closed Thursday, Nov. 26, and Friday, Nov. 27, for Thanksgiving; Saturday, Nov. 28, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Sunday, Nov. 29, from noon to 6 p.m.; and Monday, Nov. 30, and Tuesday, Dec. 1, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Election Day is Saturday, Dec. 5.

Six candidates are on the District VIII ballot: Irma Morales Lopez, Oscar “Ram” Ramirez, Mario Trevino, Priscilla “Gordiloca” Trevino, José Sergio Dorantes and José Luis Maldonado. The seat opened when Alyssa Cigarroa announced a run for mayor in August, triggering the state’s resign-to-run provision with more than a year left in her council term. The winner will serve the rest of that term.

The mayoral race is a separate election with its own ballot and its own schedule. Cigarroa, who won about 36 percent of the vote on Nov. 3, faces incumbent Mayor Victor D. Treviño, who won about 32 percent, in a runoff on Saturday, Dec. 12. Early voting for the mayoral runoff runs Monday, Nov. 30, through Tuesday, Dec. 8. The Dec. 12 ballot also includes a runoff for Laredo College Board of Trustees Position 9.

That means District VIII voters who want to take part in both elections must vote in each one separately. A ballot cast in the District VIII special election does not count toward the mayoral runoff, and vice versa. Former mayoral candidate JD Gonzalez has endorsed Treviño in the runoff, according to the Treviño campaign.

Webb Watch 956 is not endorsing any candidate in either race. Voters with questions about polling places or ballots can contact the Webb County Elections Office.

Sources: Local National, Nov. 24, 2026; Dr. Victor Treviño campaign, Nov. 23–24, 2026.
